subject: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?

messages.author: e80b0bd9c457cfc1
messages.subject: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?
parts:
Dear All, 
While I am still studying how to apply SECR to determine density and population of Cricetomys rats in an African forest, I am also wondering if it can be used to give me an estimate of "home range". It will really be helpful in my studies. Please does anyone have an idea of a paper I can look at or how to help refine my search.
I will appreciate your swift response.
Biplang

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?
parts:
Hi Yadok

SECR gives you an estimate of the spatial scale of detection (sigma). This is MUCH better than some conventional trap-revealed measures of home range size (mean maximum distance moved MMDM, asymptotic range length ARL etc.) because it adjusts for the truncation of some ranges at the edge of your trapping grid, and for sample size, BUT it is not the same thing as home range size because it depends on the willingness of animals to enter traps. I came across this nice quote a few weeks ago from Hayne (1949) (J. Mamm. 30: 1–18): “Even if  the  probability  associated  with  the  independent  action  of  a  single  trap  could  be  estimated,  this  would  be  an  index  of  trap-frequenting  activity,  and  not  of  normal  activity.  To  consider  one  type  of  activity  as  directly  reflecting  the  other  is  only  one  possible  explanation.”   SECR takes care of the first issue (action of a single trap) but not the second. SECR also usually (but not necessarily) fits a circular (radially symmetrical) model.

Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Can I use SECR to measure home range of rats?
parts:
Hi Biplang

'sigma' is a parameter in the SECR model. It is not fixed - it takes different values in different studies, and may vary within a population according to sex, time etc.

Please note that R is case-sensitive, and there is no package 'SECR'. SECR refers to a set of methods in general.

Murray
